messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU memory pressure detected — pool=pool-gpu-12 region=us-east-1 metric=GPU_MEM_UTIL > 92% for 3m :rotating_light:
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident triggered (PD-12345) — gpu-pressure-high — Assigned to mike_oncall
mike_oncall: ack
mike_oncall: Looking into it. Metrics show repeated CUDA OOMs on node g12-07, container=model-serve-8732
lucy_infra: on it, checking allocator + KV cache stats
sara_dev: any customer impact yet? :eyes:
mike_oncall: quick check: spike in 503s on /v1/generate, approx 2.8% error-rate in last 5m. Affected tenant=acme-corp
kevin_sre: tagging in. if this is a kvcache/prefetch leak, we should evict prefetchers and reprovision the node as a mitigation
mike_oncall: stacktrace from model-serve-8732 on g12-07:
```
2025-08-14T12:15:03Z ERROR cuda: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED: out of memory
... traceback ...
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2G
```
lucy_infra: running quick diagnostics:
```
ssh ops@g12-07
sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
```
mike_oncall: nvidia-smi: 15732 MiB used / 16384 MiB total. Processes: model-serve-8732 (~12.3G), prefetcher-21 (~2.7G)
sara_dev: can we kill the prefetcher? sounds like cache population stole the spare memory
lucy_infra: trying graceful eviction of prefetcher container (id=64f3a2) on g12-07
pagerduty: PagerDuty: mike_oncall acknowledged PD-12345
incident-bot: runbook match: gpu-memory-pressure v2 — suggested steps:
  1) evict background prefetchers
  2) scale pool +1 node
  3) drain non-prod traffic from affected node
  4) enable fallback model for heavy tenants
mike_oncall: evicted prefetcher (container 64f3a2) — stopping process now
lucy_infra: prefetcher stopped, memory freed. model-serve now at ~10.2G used
kevin_sre: good. initiating autoscale +1 node for pool-gpu-12 (requesting spare capacity)
mike_oncall: rerouting non-prod traffic off pool-gpu-12:
```
# command
redwoodctl route set --pool pool-gpu-12 --drain --filter "tier!=prod"
```
lucy_infra: router responded: OK — draining non-prod
sara_dev: acme-corp is prod — are they still seeing issues?
mike_oncall: acme-corp success rate recovered to 99.6% (was 96.9% at peak)
kevin_sre: monitor for 15m. if OOM recurs consider: force-quantize fallback or deploy small-ctx canary model for that tenant
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Escalation to kevin_sre triggered (notified)
kevin_sre: ack — I'm on-call for the escalation
incident-bot: Auto-adjust: throttle background prefetch heuristic for pool-gpu-12 for next 30m
lucy_infra: looked through kube events — prefetcher previously OOMKilled, likely memory leak in v0.8.2-prefetch
sara_dev: please open a bug and tag release-team. we should block next rollout until patched
mike_oncall: created ticket INF-8472 with logs + nvidia-smi dumps
sara_dev: draft customer note:
"We observed a brief increase in inference errors (~3% of requests) for /v1/generate due to GPU memory pressure on a single pool in us-east-1. We mitigated the issue by evicting a background prefetch process and adding capacity to the pool. No persistent data loss was detected."
kevin_sre: add mitigation steps + ETA to that note, we'll pass to support for outreach
sara_dev: ETA for fix: patch prefetcher memory leak in v0.8.3 targeted tomorrow morning; hotpatch available if we see recurrence tonight
mike_oncall: Monitoring dashboard: https://console.redwood/status/GPUPool/pool-gpu-12 — spike resolved
lucy_infra: added alert-suppression to avoid repeated pages from the same node for a 10m window to reduce noise
mike_oncall: handing off to next oncall (lucy_infra) in 10m — will append final notes to incident log
lucy_infra: ack handoff — watching for regressions and keeping PD on the hook
sara_dev: thanks — will close thread once stable for 30m :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident PD-12345 resolved by mike_oncall — duration 24m
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD-12345 has been resolved
mike_oncall: postmortem notes: suspected prefetcher v0.8.2 memory leak. Mitigation applied: prefetcher eviction + pool scale. Impact: transient 503s (~3%) for acme-corp. Next steps: hotfix v0.8.3 tomorrow, add kvcache circuit breaker, tighten autoscale thresholds and add prefetcher memory limit.
